cultural_entities.gloss: A highly specific, culturally resonant Hindi term describing the pleasant, earthy aroma of dry soil when first struck by rain (petrichor), carrying deep nostalgic and seasonal associations in South Asia.
cultural_entities.translation_note: Translated as 'earthy fragrance', which captures the literal sense but loses the specific cultural association with the scent of dry earth meeting the first monsoon rains.

stanzas.loss_note: The translation of 'sondhi' as 'earthy' captures the literal sense but loses the specific cultural and sensory association of the pleasant smell of dry soil wet by rain in India.

original_poem:
पिछले मौसम का फूल  
अब भी खिला है मेरे आँगन में,  
सौंधी महक फैलाए  
जैसे यादें किसी बीते पल की।  

हवा के साथ झूमता है,  
धूप में रंग बदलता है,  
मानो समय की साक्षी दे रहा हो,  
हर बीते लम्हे का गवाह बन रहा हो।  

बीत गई ऋतुएं,  
नए फूल आएंगे  
पर इसका रंग और महक  
कभी नहीं खोएगी,  
जैसे पुरानी यादों का एक कोना  
हमेशा जीवित रहेगा।
translated_poem:
The flower of the past season  
Still blooms in my courtyard,  
Spreading an earthy fragrance,  
Like memories of a moment gone by.

It sways with the breeze,  
Changes color in the sunlight,  
As if bearing witness to time,  
Standing as a testament to each passing moment.

Seasons will pass,  
New flowers will come,  
But its color and scent  
Will never fade,  
Like a corner of old memories  
That will forever stay alive.
